questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ undergoes a one-dimensional head-on elastic collision with a stationary particle of mass $3m$. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy transferred to the stationary particle is
questions.explanationEn: In a 1D elastic collision with a stationary target $m_2$, the final velocity of the projectile $m_1$ is $v_1' = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v = \frac{m - 3m}{4m}v = -\frac{v}{2}$. Thus $m_1$ retains $\left(\frac{v_1'}{v}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}$ of its initial kinetic energy, and transfers $1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$ to $m_2$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The radius of gyration of a uniform solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its longitudinal symmetry axis is
questions.explanationEn: The moment of inertia of a solid cylinder about its symmetry axis is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = Mk^2$, which gives the radius of gyration $k = \frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble of radius $R$ and surface tension $T$ (in air) is
questions.explanationEn: A soap bubble in air has two liquid–air interfaces (inner and outer), each contributing $\frac{2T}{R}$ to the Laplace pressure difference. Therefore, the total excess pressure inside is $\Delta P = \frac{4T}{R}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: For an isotropic homogeneous elastic solid, the Young's modulus $Y$, bulk modulus $K$, and shear modulus $\eta$ are related by
questions.explanationEn: From $Y = 2\eta(1 + \sigma)$ and $Y = 3K(1 - 2\sigma)$, eliminating Poisson's ratio $\sigma$ gives $\frac{3}{Y} + \frac{1}{3K} = \frac{1}{\eta} + \dots$, specifically $2\left(\frac{Y}{2\eta} - 1\right) + \left(1 - \frac{Y}{3K}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{Y}{\eta} + \frac{Y}{3K} = 3 \implies \frac{9}{Y} = \frac{3}{\eta} + \frac{1}{K}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A rotating uniform spherical star of radius $R$ and angular velocity $\omega$ collapses symmetrically under its own gravity to a uniform sphere of radius $R/2$ without any mass loss or external torque. Its new angular velocity is
questions.explanationEn: With no external torque, angular momentum $L = I\omega$ is conserved. Since $I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2 \propto R^2$, halving $R$ reduces $I$ to $I/4$, so $\omega' = 4\omega$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform solid cylinder is released from rest on an inclined plane of inclination $\theta$. The minimum coefficient of static friction $\mu_s$ required for the cylinder to roll without slipping is
questions.explanationEn: For pure rolling, $Mg\sin\theta - f = Ma$ and $fR = I\alpha = \left(\frac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\frac{a}{R} \implies f = \frac{1}{2}Ma$. Thus $a = \frac{2}{3}g\sin\theta$ and $f = \frac{1}{3}Mg\sin\theta$. Requiring $f \le \mu_s N = \mu_s Mg\cos\theta$ gives $\mu_s \ge \frac{1}{3}\tan\theta$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform circular ring and a uniform solid circular disc of the same radius are released simultaneously from rest from the top of an inclined plane and roll without slipping. The ratio of the time taken by the ring to that taken by the disc to reach the bottom is
questions.explanationEn: Since $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + \beta}$ (where $\beta = I/(MR^2)$) and $t = \sqrt{\frac{2s}{a}} \propto \sqrt{1 + \beta}$, we have $\beta_{\text{ring}} = 1$ and $\beta_{\text{disc}} = \frac{1}{2}$. Thus $\frac{t_{\text{ring}}}{t_{\text{disc}}} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 1}{1 + 1/2}} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: When $27$ identical spherical liquid droplets, each of radius $r$ and surface tension $T$, coalesce isothermally into a single large spherical drop, the surface energy released is
questions.explanationEn: By volume conservation, $R^3 = 27r^3 \implies R = 3r$. The decrease in surface area is $\Delta A = 27(4\pi r^2) - 4\pi(3r)^2 = (108 - 36)\pi r^2 = 72\pi r^2$. Thus, the surface energy released is $T\Delta A = 72\pi r^2 T$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: From a uniform circular disc of original mass $M$ and radius $R$, a circular hole of radius $R/2$ is cut out such that the circumference of the hole passes through the center $O$ of the original disc. The moment of inertia of the remaining portion about an axis through $O$ perpendicular to the plane of the disc is
questions.explanationEn: The removed disc has mass $m_h = M\left(\frac{R/2}{R}\right)^2 = \frac{M}{4}$ and its center is at distance $d = \frac{R}{2}$ from $O$. By the parallel-axis theorem, its moment of inertia about $O$ is $I_h = \frac{1}{2}m_h(R/2)^2 + m_h(R/2)^2 = \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{M}{4}\right)\frac{R^2}{4} = \frac{3}{32}MR^2$. Subtracting from $I_{\text{full}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{16}{32}MR^2$ gives $I_{\text{rem}} = \frac{13}{32}MR^2$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Two horizontal capillary tubes of equal length $L$ and radii $r$ and $2r$ are connected in series. A viscous liquid flows steadily through the combination under a total pressure difference $\Delta P$. The pressure drop across the narrower tube (radius $r$) is
questions.explanationEn: From Poiseuille's law, the hydraulic resistance is $R_H = \frac{8\eta L}{\pi r^4} \propto r^{-4}$, so $R_{H1} = 16 R_{H2}$. Since the volume flow rate $Q$ is the same in both tubes in series, $\Delta P_1 = \frac{R_{H1}}{R_{H1} + R_{H2}}\Delta P = \frac{16}{17}\Delta P$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about surface tension and capillarity is/are correct?
optionsEn: If the contact angle $\theta$ between a liquid and a capillary tube wall is obtuse ($\theta > 90^\circ$), the liquid level is depressed inside the capillary
Surface tension of most pure liquids decreases with increasing temperature and vanishes at the critical temperature
The excess pressure inside a smaller air bubble in water is greater than that inside a larger air bubble at the same depth
A spherical liquid drop in air has twice the excess pressure of a soap bubble of the same radius and same surface tension
questions.explanationEn: (B) True: Higher temperature weakens intermolecular cohesion, reducing $T \to 0$ at $T_c$. (A) True: $h = \frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r} < 0$ when $\theta > 90^\circ$ (e.g., mercury in glass). (C) True: $\Delta P = \frac{2T}{R}$ is inversely proportional to $R$. (D) False: A soap bubble has two surfaces ($\frac{4T}{R}$), which is twice that of a liquid drop ($\frac{2T}{R}$), not half. Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A rocket of instantaneous mass $M(t)$ ascends vertically upward from the Earth's surface (uniform downward gravity $g$) by ejecting exhaust gas downward at a constant relative speed $u$ and constant mass burn rate $\alpha = -\frac{dM}{dt} > 0$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: For the rocket to lift off from the launch pad ($M = M_0$), we must have $\alpha u > M_0 g$
The upward thrust force acting on the rocket is $F_{\text{thrust}} = \alpha u$
As fuel burns and $M(t)$ decreases (at constant $\alpha$ and $u$), the upward acceleration decreases
The instantaneous upward acceleration is $a(t) = \frac{\alpha u}{M(t)} - g$
questions.explanationEn: The equation of motion is $M\frac{dv}{dt} = \alpha u - Mg$, so thrust is $\alpha u$ (A is true), lift-off requires $\alpha u > M_0 g$ (B is true), and $a(t) = \frac{\alpha u}{M(t)} - g$ (C is true). As $M(t)$ decreases, $\frac{\alpha u}{M(t)}$ increases, so acceleration increases (D is false). Hence, options (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $m$ moves in one dimension under the potential energy $U(x) = x^4 - 2x^2$ (in SI units). Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: $x = 0$ is a position of unstable equilibrium
For total energy $E = -0.5\text{ J}$, the particle can cross $x = 0$
The minimum value of the potential energy is $-1\text{ J}$
$x = +1$ and $x = -1$ are positions of stable equilibrium
questions.explanationEn: Setting $U'(x) = 4x^3 - 4x = 4x(x^2 - 1) = 0$ gives equilibria at $x = 0, \pm 1$. Computing $U''(x) = 12x^2 - 4$: at $x = 0$, $U''(0) = -4 < 0$ (unstable, A is true); at $x = \pm 1$, $U''(\pm 1) = +8 > 0$ (stable, B is true) with $U(\pm 1) = 1 - 2 = -1\text{ J}$ (C is true). Since $U(0) = 0 > E = -0.5\text{ J}$, the region around $x = 0$ is classically forbidden (D is false). Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about elastic deformation of rods and beams is/are correct?
optionsEn: The bulk modulus of an ideal gas in an isothermal process equals its pressure $P$
In a bent horizontal beam, the neutral surface experiences neither longitudinal tension nor longitudinal compression
For the same mass, length, and material, a hollow cylindrical shaft can withstand a larger twisting torque per unit angle of twist than a solid cylindrical shaft
The shear modulus of an ideal inviscid fluid is infinite
questions.explanationEn: (C) True: A hollow shaft distributes mass at larger radii, increasing the polar moment of area $J = \frac{\pi}{2}(R_o^4 - R_i^4)$ and torsional rigidity. (B) True: By definition, the neutral surface has zero longitudinal strain. (A) True: At constant $T$, $PV = \text{const} \implies K_T = -V\left(\frac{\partial P}{\partial V}\right)_T = P$. (D) False: An ideal fluid cannot sustain static shear stress, so its shear modulus is zero. Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A rocket engine ejects exhaust gases at a speed of $2500\text{ m/s}$ relative to the rocket at a constant mass burn rate of $4\text{ kg/s}$. The thrust produced by the engine, in $\text{kN}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: $F_{\text{thrust}} = u\left|\frac{dm}{dt}\right| = 2500 \times 4 = 10{,}000\text{ N} = 10\text{ kN}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A flat plate of area $0.5\text{ m}^2$ moves at a steady speed of $2\text{ m/s}$ over a stationary parallel plate separated by a $5\text{ mm}$ thick layer of oil of viscosity $\eta = 0.1\text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$. Assuming a linear velocity profile, the viscous drag force on the moving plate, in $\text{N}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Newton's law of viscosity, $F = \eta A \frac{v}{d} = (0.1)(0.5)\frac{2}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = 20\text{ N}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A clean vertical glass capillary tube of inner radius $0.5\text{ mm}$ is dipped in water (surface tension $T = 0.0735\text{ N/m}$, density $\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3$, contact angle $\theta = 0^\circ$). Taking $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the height to which water rises in the tube, in $\text{cm}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: $h = \frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r} = \frac{2(0.0735)(1)}{1000 \times 9.8 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}} = 0.03\text{ m} = 3\text{ cm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A horizontal turntable of moment of inertia $2\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$ rotates freely at $12\text{ rad/s}$ about its vertical axis. A stationary coaxial ring of moment of inertia $1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$ is gently dropped onto it. The final common angular speed, in $\text{rad/s}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By conservation of angular momentum, $I_1 \omega_1 = (I_1 + I_2)\omega_f \implies \omega_f = \frac{2 \times 12}{2 + 1} = 8\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $4\text{ kg}$ rolls without slipping on a horizontal floor with a center-of-mass speed of $3\text{ m/s}$. Its total kinetic energy, in $\text{J}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: For a solid cylinder ($I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$), $K_{\text{tot}} = \frac{1}{2}Mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\frac{v}{R}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4}Mv^2 = \frac{3}{4}(4)(3^2) = 27\text{ J}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A rocket of total initial mass $1000\text{ kg}$ (including fuel) starts from rest in gravity-free deep space and ejects exhaust gases at a constant relative speed of $2.0\text{ km/s}$. When $750\text{ kg}$ of fuel has been burned, the speed of the rocket, in $\text{km/s}$, is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The remaining mass is $M_f = 1000 - 750 = 250\text{ kg}$. By Tsiolkovsky's rocket equation, $v = u\ln\left(\frac{M_0}{M_f}\right) = 2.0\ln\left(\frac{1000}{250}\right) = 2.0\ln 4 \approx 2.77\text{ km/s}$.
